title: fix(plugin-approvals): a new delegation starts with the Delegator set to you, and its help says why
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuACdPWFJTLDcTrByFCHLzqb)_

Fixes #25342

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What

Setup → Delegations (OOO): the Delegator of `sys_approval_delegation` only ever offers the signed-in user, because `bindDelegationWriteGuard` admits nobody else. The field still opened at "Select…", and a search for a colleague answered "No options found" with no reason.

- `delegator_id` now declares `defaultValue: 'current_user'`. A new delegation starts with its one admissible Delegator filled in.
- The field's help now says why: "The user going out of office. You can delegate only your own approvals, so this is always you: it starts as you and offers no one else. Their individually-routed approver slots are rerouted while active."
- The `lookupFilters`, the write guard and the approval-service filter are unchanged. `organization_id` is not touched; queued #25280 edits that field's help.

## Why this spelling

I checked how the platform defaults a person field to the current user, on `origin/main` `830a63a680`:

- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` `defaultValue` says `current_user` is legal "on `user` or `lookup` with `reference: 'sys_user'` only". The spec's token table is `defaultValueTokenIssue` in `packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts`, and the constant is `DEFAULT_VALUE_TOKEN_CURRENT_USER` in `default-value-tokens.ts`.
- The engine resolves it at insert time to the acting user's id: `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, the `isCurrentUserDefaultToken` branch of the field-default pass. With no authenticated user it leaves the field unset.
- The one in-repo declaration is `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/field-zoo.object.ts` `f_owner` (`Field.user({ defaultValue: 'current_user' })`). No other platform object defaults a lookup to the current user, so this is the first such platform field. It uses the spelling the spec, the engine and the docs (`content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`) all name.

`packages/spec` is not edited.

## Translations

- `en` was regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write`.
- `es-ES` and `ja-JP` were byte copies of the old English help. They now carry translations, and the next extract dropped their two `source-hashes` entries.
- `zh-CN` already had a translated help, so I updated it to the new meaning too. It has no hash entry, so nothing would have flagged it as stale.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-delegation-delegator-picker.test.ts` keeps every existing pin. It gains one for the default: the declaration and the registered body carry `DEFAULT_VALUE_TOKEN_CURRENT_USER`, and a full `FieldSchema.safeParse` of the field is green, so the spec admits the token on this lookup.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: Test Files 94 passed (94), Tests 1215 passed (1215).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` reports OK.
- Ablation: deleting `defaultValue: 'current_user',` (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor x1 -> x0) turned the new pin red (`expected undefined to be 'current_user'`, 1 failed | 9 passed). The file was restored to its HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` was empty. The test imports the object from `src/`, so no build was needed. My first attempt was a refused anchor miss, so nothing ran on it.
- Derived gate families: run locally on this head. The PR's check-runs carry the full set.

## Acceptance notes

- **The console's form prefill is NOT MEASURED.** objectui answers 403 from this container, so I could not read how its create form treats a `current_user` default. The server side is pinned. If the console does not prefill from this token, that gap belongs to objectui and would hit the showcase `f_owner` field too. It is not a reason to change the spelling here.
- Server-side writes behave as before. The engine default and the write guard's omitted-delegator stamp both name the acting user. A system write with no user still leaves the field unset, so `required` refuses it, and the existing pin holds that.
